localBiteReport: The most recent available reports for Choctawhatchee Bay are from roughly one week ago (early November 2026), not same-day. Water temperature at this location is 71°F as of today. On FishingBooker's Choctawhatchee Bay feed, an angler reported catching a couple of solid redfish under the bridge area about seven days ago, with baitfish also active in the bay. On captainexperiences.com, a Freeport-based guide (Alex S.) reported about one week ago that king mackerel have moved in, while a Santa Rosa Beach guide noted the bite has been a mix of live bait early morning and soft plastics throughout the day — consistent with the fall redfish and speckled trout pattern typical of this time of year. Half Hitch Tackle's Destin blog confirmed a new report dated November 9 exists (their most current), though its full bay-specific content was not accessible via search; their November 2 report and broader seasonal context suggest sheepshead are picking up around bridge structure as water cools, redfish remain active on the flats, and speckled trout are a secondary target in creek and bayou mouths.
